entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nikephoros Tarchaneiotes was a 13th-century Byzantine aristocrat and general, born into the influential Tarchaneiotes family, who played a significant role in the Byzantine–Latin Wars. He served as a military commander under Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and led key campaigns against the Latin Empire in Constantinople. Tarchaneiotes' military successes helped secure Byzantine control over the city and contributed to the empire's survival for several decades.

Tarchaneiotes' legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Orthodox Church. His contributions to the arts, particularly in the realm of architecture and liturgical iconography, helped preserve Byzantine cultural heritage during a tumultuous period in the empire's history.

The Tarchaneiotes family's influence on Byzantine politics and culture continues to be felt today, with many historians noting the family's role in shaping the empire's response to the Latin Empire's rise to power.
